newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army moves to retake area around camp.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army moves to retake area around camp.

text.p: Sri Lankan armed forces have launched an operation to clear areas near an eastern security forces camp overrun by separatist Tamil Tiger guerrillas on Wednesday, a military spokesman said on Thursday.
"No sooner (than) reinforcements established themselves in the camp, we launched an operation to flush out terrorists from the vicinity," the spokesman told Reuters.
In a pre-dawn attack on Wednesday, the Tigers overran the camp at Pulukunava in eastern Batticaloa district, about 200 km (125 miles) from Colombo, local security officials said.
It was the Tigers' biggest attack on government forces in more than two months.
The attack by more than 500 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels killed 36 security personnel and two civilian helpers and wounded 37 more, the military spokesman said.
"LTTE tramsmissions monitored by forces indicated 34 of their cadres had been killed in the attack, but we believe the final tally may be much higher," he said.
The rebels were not immediately available for comment.
Military officials said the camp was occupied by about 120 men, mostly police commandos and some artillerymen.
Government reinforcements retook the camp on Wednesday and reestablished themselves in parts of it not destroyed by the Tigers.
The Tigers are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils, most of whom are Hindus, in the north and the east of this predominantly Buddhist Sinhalese nation.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The Tigers say the toll is much higher.
